value_stream.name: Construction Project Material Staging & Phased Delivery

fields.Frequency: Per project; ~80–120 active B2B projects (of which ~20–30 are large staged/phased material projects)
fields.Participants: Trade Sales Mgr, Category Managers, Supply Planning, Procurement
fields.Trigger: Contractor engages BuildRight for project supply

Automation Opportunity: - Material-takeoff auto-computed from the project dimensions; quotation auto-generated from the takeoff × pricing; project-status auto-tracked from milestone completion
Controls: - CTL-460 (ensure controlled execution — Project Material Planning & Phasing (PA-77.1).)
- operational: Trade Sales Manager sign-off on the workflow output
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scope-creep risk**: the project scope expands beyond the original quotation, eroding margin; mitigated by the change-order process and the scope-confirmation sign-off

- **Data-quality risk**: incomplete or inaccurate master data (pricing, inventory, customer) corrupts the workflow output; mitigated by the master-data governance (VS-29 / W291) and the periodic audit
System Touchpoints: - Project/design (links to VS-11 / W58 corporate account, VS-66 / W211 design)
- Logistics/DC (links to VS-04 / W3 receiving, VS-04 / W52 fleet, VS-77 / material staging)
- Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113)
Time Estimate: - Frequency: Per project; ~80–120 active B2B projects (of which ~20–30 are large staged/phased material projects)
- Absorbed into the Trade Sales Manager role; not incremental headcount unless volume scales significantly.

steps.activity: Trade Sales Manager works with contractor: reviews blueprint and bill of quantities, identifies BuildRight-supplied categories, estimates quantities per phase
Supply Planning validates availability: checks inventory vs. requirements, identifies long-lead items (imported tiles: 60–90 days), raises advance POs
Trade Sales Manager produces phased delivery schedule: divides project into phases, allocates quantities, aligns delivery dates with timeline; obtains contractor sign-off

steps.activity: Supply Planner creates inventory reservations: allocates stock against project PO, prevents ROP from consuming project stock; configures ATP for uncommitted availability
Category Manager monitors reservations: ensures no stockouts for regular customers, adjusts allocation, authorizes substitutions when unavailable
DC Ops segregates project inventory: dedicated staging area per project, labels with project reference, coordinates delivery scheduling per phase

steps.activity: Trade Sales Rep identifies substitution need: out of stock, discontinued, import delay; proposes alternative from available inventory
Category Manager evaluates: technical equivalence, visual equivalence (tiles/fixtures), price difference, contractor approval; documents rationale
Contractor approves/rejects: if approved — updates reservation and PO; if rejected — Procurement expedites original; all documented in project file

workflows.name: Project Material Price Lock & Escalation Management

Automation Opportunity: - Pricing auto-computed from the cost + margin target; settlement auto-reconciled with discrepancy-flagging; invoice auto-generated from the POD/delivery record
Controls: - CTL-460 (price-change authorization — links to VS-08 / W40); Operational: Trade Sales Manager sign-off on the workflow output
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-erosion risk**: pricing miscalculation (commission, discount, surcharge) erodes net margin below target; mitigated by the margin-floor guard and pre-launch validation

- **Data-quality risk**: incomplete or inaccurate master data (pricing, inventory, customer) corrupts the workflow output; mitigated by the master-data governance (VS-29 / W291) and the periodic audit
System Touchpoints: - Pricing/financials (links to VS-17 / W9 financial close, VS-29 / W289 pricing master)
- Project/design (links to VS-11 / W58 corporate account, VS-66 / W211 design)
- Logistics/DC (links to VS-04 / W3 receiving, VS-04 / W52 fleet, VS-77 / material staging)
Time Estimate: - Volume: ~80–120 active B2B projects (of which ~20–30 are large staged/phased material projects)
- Absorbed into the Trade Sales Manager role; not incremental headcount unless volume scales significantly.

steps.activity: Trade Sales Manager negotiates price lock: fixed price for project duration (3–12 months) or escalation formula tied to published index, with maximum cap
Pricing Analyst monitors market movements vs. locked prices: identifies margin erosion risk; quantifies impact; escalates if margin falls below 15%
Finance tracks project margin: revenue vs. actual cost including price lock impact, holding cost, delivery cost; reports monthly to VP Merchandising

steps.activity: Trade Sales Rep documents quality specs: material grades, tile PEI ratings, lumber species/grade/moisture, fixture brand/model/finish
Category Manager verifies product availability matching specs: confirms grades and brands, identifies special orders, provides certification documents (PS mark, ASTM, ISO)
Quality provides test certificates for project documentation: cement compressive strength, steel tensile strength, tile breaking strength; includes in project package

workflows.name: Project Account Credit & Payment Terms Management

Automation Opportunity: - Credit-score auto-computed from the financial-data feed; credit-limit auto-suggested from the scoring model; collection-aging auto-tracked with escalation
Controls: - CTL-212: trade-credit authorization & exposure guard — links to VS-16 / W24; Operational: Trade Sales Manager sign-off on the workflow output
Pain Points / Risks: - **Credit-default risk**: a trade account defaults on extended credit, creating a bad-debt write-off; mitigated by the credit-scoring model and the credit-limit monitoring

- **Phase-mismatch risk**: material arrives ahead of the construction phase needing it (or late), inflating staging cost and delaying the project; mitigated by the phasing plan tied to the construction schedule
System Touchpoints: - Pricing/financials (links to VS-17 / W9 financial close, VS-29 / W289 pricing master)
- Compliance/risk (links to VS-22 / regulatory, VS-86 / AML, VS-91 / privacy)
- Project/design (links to VS-11 / W58 corporate account, VS-66 / W211 design)
Time Estimate: - Volume: ~80–120 active B2B projects (of which ~20–30 are large staged/phased material projects)
- Absorbed into the Trade Sales Manager role; not incremental headcount unless volume scales significantly.

steps.activity: Trade Sales Manager negotiates payment terms: milestone-based, progress billing, retention (5–10%), credit terms (Net 30/60); Credit Manager approval per authorization matrix
Finance sets up project billing: creates project account, links phase delivery to billing milestones, configures retention tracking, establishes credit limit
Trade Sales Manager monitors payment health: tracks billed vs. collected, escalates overdue payments, ensures retention release upon completion
